summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 2, part 87), narrator Cas Russell parts ways with Tresting in a rundown neighborhood after a tense exchange in which Tresting urges him to change his ways. Alone, Russell reflects that he has begun to care about Arthur despite himself, and resolves to stop. He walks, rides the LA metro to Union Station, and disguises himself with a tourist T-shirt, cap, sunglasses and tote bag to hide his bruises.
one_line: Cas Russell parts ways with Tresting, admits he has started to care about Arthur, and disguises himself at Union Station in LA.
key_facts: Tresting tells Russell that Pithica is after him, along with the police and the unnamed guys who want something from Russell.
Russell pulls off the freeway and parks the van in the seediest-looking neighborhood he can find.
Tresting wipes his door handle and seatbelt with a napkin as he gets out of the van.
Tresting thanks Russell for saving his life back at his office, and Russell replies, "We're even."
Tresting tells Russell, "You're a good kid. You ain't gotta be like this."
Russell tells Tresting, "I like how I am just fine."
Russell reflects that Dawna Polk would have known how to say exactly the right thing so that Arthur understood her.
Russell admits to himself that he had started to care about Arthur, and resolves to stop caring.
Russell takes the Los Angeles metro line up to Union Station, choosing to travel legally for once.
At a tourist stand in Union Station, Russell buys an "I ♥ LA" T-shirt, a baseball cap, sunglasses, and a tote bag.
Russell changes clothes in a restroom, and the sunglasses cover most of the bruising on his face.
